MA4804.title: Optimization Theory And Applications
MA4804.description: Introduction and Overview; Fundamental Concepts in Optimization; Categorization of Optimization Problems and Methods; Non-Linear Programming; Linear Programming; Discrete Optimization; Software Tools; Multi-Objective Optimization.

MA4811.title: Psychrometry And Air Conditioning
MA4811.description: Air-conditioning systems and applications. Psychrometrics, comfort and health. Heat transmission in building structures, heat gains, and cooling load calculations. Cooling equipment. Chilled water distribution systems. Air distribution systems. Cooling systems design sizing and energy calculations. Computer-aided load sizing of air-conditioning system.

MA4825.title: Robotics
MA4825.description: Introduction to robotics. Robot actuators and sensing systems. Fundamentals of rigid body motion. Kinematics of robot manipulators. Motion planning and programming. Dynamics and control of robot manipulators. Robotics design and applications

MA4830.title: Realtime Software For Mechatronic Systems
MA4830.description: Review of Foundation & Advanced C Techniques. Fundamentals of Realtime Systems Concepts. Software System Design.

MA4832.title: Microprocessor Systems
MA4832.description: Fundamental of microprocessor architecture. Concepts and techniques of memory organisation, stacks and the use of interrupts. Data representation and operation. Programming. Timers and I/O operations. Basic and display electronics. Interfacing to digital devices.

MA4838.title: Non-Conventional Manufacturing Processes
MA4838.description:
This course will cover the subject of non-conventional manufacturing processes- an area which has relevance to industries such as biomedical, aerospace and precision engineering.
The course will begin by comparing non-conventional processes with the more traditional manufacturing approaches. This will be followed by each of the main removal mechanisms (mechanical, chemical and thermal) being presented along with their advantages, limitations and applications.
The combination of these techniques amongst themselves or with more traditional machining processes will be covered under hybrid processes.
The course will conclude with a series of case studies reinforcing the proliferation of these processes in industry.

MA4842.title: Engineering Metrology
MA4842.notAvailableToProgramme: ME(DES)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(DES)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), MEEC(DES)(2011-onwards), MEEC(MEC)(2011-onwards)
MA4842.description:
Metrology is an important topic covering all aspects of engineering and science. This course will focus on introducing the students to the fundamentals of measurement including topics such as why we measure, the SI system as well as the terminology used. Calibration has long been a neglected area of measurement but with the rapid adoption of ISO quality standards the need to demonstrate the frequency and method of calibration has taken on added importance.
The main areas of metrology which are relevant to mechanical engineers are mechanical, surface, dimensional and optical metrology. These four areas will be addressed with detailed coverage of the principles, the instrumentation and their application. 
The course will also place significant importance on the case studies as a way of reinforcing the concept as well as demonstrating their widespread use in industry. Some of the case studies will look at historical examples of famous metrological failures, various measurement examples as well as industry-based problems.

MA4843.title: Management Of Product Development
MA4843.notAvailableAsBdeueToProgramme: ACBS, ACC, ADM, AERO, ASEC, BCE, BCG, BEEC, BIE, BMS, BS, BUS, CBE, CBEC, CE, CEE, CEEC, CHEM, CHIN, CS, CSC, CSEC, CVEC, ECON, EEE, EEEC, EESS, ELH, ENE, ENEC, ENG, HIST, IEEC, IEM, LMS, MAEC, MAT, MATH, ME, ME(DES), ME(MEC), MEEC, MEEC(DES), MEEC(MEC), MS, MS-2ndMaj/Spec(MSB), MTEC, PHIL, PHY, PPGA, PSY, REP, SOC, SSM
MA4843.description:
Product development is an integrated process of marketing, engineering and production and effective management of the product development ensures that quality products are launched on time. It focuses on planning processes, identifying customer needs, defining the product specifications, generating concepts, concept selection and testing and organizational support. This course provides CoE undergraduates with a deep understanding of product development concepts and equips them with skills to manage the various stages of product development.
This course connects new product development to management issues on concept generation, selection, development and evaluation. This course also includes innovative management, product/brand strategy so the student can acquire knowledge about new product development needed when they start work.

MA4844.title: Industrial Design
MA4844.notAvailableToProgramme: ME(DES)(2004-2010)(Non Direct Entry), ME(DES)(2004-2011)(Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), MEEC(DES)(2004-2010)(Non Direct Entry), MEEC(DES)(2004-2011)(Direct Entry)
MA4844.description: The course contains 39 hours allocated to lectures with take-home assignments to reinforce learning of the principles and practice of industrial design. MA4845.title: Manufacturing Automation

MA4847.title: Human Factors Engineering
MA4847.description: This course is designed to develop an understanding of human anatomy, physiology, and psychology as well as modern manufacturing technology and work organization. It provides a multidisciplinary background in these basic areas, as well as their application to the practical problems in ergonomics and safety that are encountered in industrial and service environments.

MA4849.title: Operations Research
MA4849.description: Refresher on probability models; Decision-making under uncertainty; Utility and risk analysis; Forecasting; Queuing models; Inventory models, planning and control; linear and integer programming; transportation and assignment problems; network optimization; Application to manufacturing, logistics and healthcare systems.

MA4850.description: Introduction to supply chain management; Value of information; Multi-echelon Inventory models; Supply Chain strategies; Supply chain and logistics network design; Warehousing and transportation management; SC benchmarking and performance measurement.

MA4856.title: Naval Architecture And Marine Engineering
MA4856.description: This course introduces Ship Layout & Stability, Ship Structural Strength, Ship Resistance, Ship Propulsion, Marine Power Plants, Advanced Power Plant Technologies, and Ship Service Systems.

MH3101.title: Complex Analysis
MH3101.description:

Analytic functions of one complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations. Contour integrals, Cauchy's theorem and Cauchy's integral formula, maximum modulus theorem, Liouville's theorem, fundamental theorem of algebra, Morera's theorem. MH3210.title: Number Theory

Review of modular arithmetic. Chinese remainder theorem. Fermat's little theorem, Wilson's theorem. Number-theoretic functions: T,O, Euler's -function, Mobius inversion formula. Legendre's symbols, quadratic reciprocity law. Continued fractions, Pell's equations. 
Primality tests and factorization of integers, RSA cryptosystem.

* One-way and two-way factorial experiments, random and fixed effects models

MH3512.title: Stochastic Processes
MH3512.description:
The objective of this course is to introduce modeling dependence. 
* Discrete-time Markov chains, examples of discrete-time Markov chains, classification of states, irreducibility, periodicity, first passage times, recurrence and transience, convergence theorems and stationary distributions
* Random walk, Poisson processes

MH3600.title: Knots And Surfaces:Introduction To Topology
MH3600.description: The topics covered include a selection of the following. Continuous functions. Surfaces. Euler characteristic. Maps and graphs. Vector fields on surfaces. Fundamental group of a surface. Knots.

MH4200.title: Abstract Algebra II
MH4200.description:
Further topics in groups, rings and fields are discussed in this course. 
1. Sylow's Theorems, Abelian groups 
2. Homomorphisms of rings, factor rings, prime and maximal ideals 
3. Unique factorization domains, Euclidean domains, principal ideal domains 
4. Modules, submodules, homomorphisms, quotient modules, modules over principal ideal domains

MH4311.title: Cryptography
MH4311.description:
Classical ciphers, cryptanalysis, linear complexity. 
Data Encryption Standard. RSA cryptosystem, primality testing and factorization of integers. Discrete logarithms. Signatures, Digital Signature Standard.

MH4320.title: Computational Economics
MH4320.description:
"Introduction to the background of Game Theory
"Introduction to the basics of the Theory of Computation
"Computation of equilibria (Nash equilibrium, market equilibrium, Walrasian equilibrium etc.)
"Algorithmic Mechanism Design
"Auction Theory (Vickrey auction, combinatorial auctions, digital-goods auctions, sponsored search auctions)
"Profit maximization
"Cost sharing mechanisms

MH4510.title: Data Mining
MH4510.description:
The course gives an overall view of the modern statistical techniques for analyzing large data sets. 

Neural networks, support vector machines, classification trees and boosting.

MH4511.title: Sampling & Survey
MH4511.description:
This course gives an introduction to sampling and the design of sample surveys. 
* Ratio and regression estimators under simple random sampling, separate and combined estimators for stratified random sampling
* Systematic sampling and its relationship with stratified and cluster sampling
* Further aspects of stratified sampling, cluster sampling with clusters of unequal sizes
* Subsampling; multi-stage sampling
* Complex sample designs

MH4513.title: Survival Analysis
MH4513.description: Examples of survival data analysis, types of censoring, parametric survival distributions (exponential, Weibull, lognormal), nonparametric methods, Kaplan-Meier estimator, tests of hypotheses, graphical methods of survival distribution fitting, goodness of fit tests.

MH4700.title: Numerical Analysis II
MH4700.description:
MAS423 is useful but not essential.

This course is to provide numerical solutions of differential equations using finite difference methods and to understand the implementation of the numerical computations using computer software packages such as MATLAB. 
* Finite difference formulae, consistency of difference schemes, finite difference methods for ordinary differential equations, classification of second-order partial differential equations, first and second order characteristics
* Matrix method and von Neumann method for stability analysis, Lax's equivalence theorem for convergence, method of characteristics
* Application to heat equation, wave equation and Poisson's equation.

MH4701.title: Mathematical Programming
MH4701.description: Unconstrained optimization: one-dimensional search, gradient method, Newton-Raphson method. Constrained optimization: feasible direction methods, penalty/barrier function methods, modern interior point methods for convex programming. Discrete optimization: formulations, cutting plane methods, branch-and-bound methods, Lagrangian relaxation, dynamic programming approach.

ML0001.title: Absolute Basics For Career
ML0001.notAvailableToProgramme: ACBS, ACC, ADM 1, BMS(2004-2014), BS(2014), BUS, CHEM(2014), CHIN 1, ECON 1, ELH 1, HIST 1, LMS 1, MAEC(2014), MATH(2014), PHY(2014), PPGA 1, PSY 1, SOC 1, SSM(2004-2014)
ML0001.description:
In today's competitive world, it is essential that students learn the crucial career skills early to ensure a competitive edge sharpened with a heightened sense of workplace values and ethics. This course takes students through a journey of career discovery, understanding and polishing of oneself which will then be translated into job application tools such as resumes and interview skills. 

All students will have the opportunity to undergo a robust Career Assessment Tool, which assesses their career options and career self and helps them chart a career action plan. They will also learn how to identify and articulate the concept of personal branding and applying that to resumes and interviews and online social media. Students will also be exposed to the basics of grooming to ensure that they are aware of the importance of first impressions in all situations.

MP2011.title: Engineering Graphics And Machine Components
MP2011.description: Orthographic projections. Pictorial views and technical sketching. Drawing standards and practices. Sectional views and machine drawings. Development of surfaces. Power transmission components. Dimensions and tolerances, surface finish. Bearings. Threaded fasteners, power screw, joints.

MP3001.title: Dynamics & Control
MP3001.notAvailableToProgramme: ME(2012-onwards), ME(MEC)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry)
MP3001.notAvailableAsCoreToProgramme: ME(DES) 2, ME(DES) 3, ME(DES) 4, MEEC(DES) 2, MEEC(DES) 3, MEEC(DES) 4, MEEC(DES) 5
MP3001.description: Modelling of linear systems. Dynamics response analysis. Theory of linear feedback control systems. Time and frequency domain design techniques. Performance and stability analysis.

MP3011.title: Engineering Design
MP3011.notAvailableAsCoreToProgramme: ENG, ENG(ME), ME(DES) 2, ME(DES) 3, ME(DES) 4, MEEC(DES) 2, MEEC(DES) 3, MEEC(DES) 4, MEEC(DES) 5
MP3011.description: Brakes and clutches. Couplings. Hydraulic power transmission. Electrical control of hydraulic circuits. Electric motors. Machine frame design. The design process: product idea and design specification. Conceptual design. Embodiment and detailed design.

MP4007.description: Our country. Engineers in society. Our world in the new Millennium.

MP4008.title: Human Resource Management
MP4008.notAvailableToProgramme: ME(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(2012-onwards), ME(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), ME(DES)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(DES)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry)

Fundamentals of Leadership. HRM Skills of a Leader: Developing, Appraising and Rewarding Staff. Managing Performance: Corporate, Group and Individual. Productivity Innovation, Creativity and Inventive Culture. Internationalization and HRM. Managing Industrial Relations. Personal Career Development. Topical HRM Issues.

MP4012.title: Design Optimization And Analysis
MP4012.notAvailableToProgramme: ME(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(2012-onwards), ME(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), ME(DES)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(DES)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2011-onwards)(Non Direct Entry), ME(MEC)(2012-onwards)(Direct Entry)
MP4012.description: Basic concepts of the finite element method. One-dimensional finite elements. Two-dimensional finite elements and modelling. Fundamental concepts in optimization. Optimization techniques.

MS0002.title: Engineers & Society
MS0002.description: Our country. Engineers and Society. Our World in the New Millennium.

MS1013.title: Materials Chemistry I
MS1013.description: Basic concepts. Chemical equilibrium. Acids and bases, activity. Electrochemistry. Reaction kinetics. Organic structure, bonding and reactions. Aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbon. Other organic families.

MS1015.title: Materials Science
MS1015.description: Introduction. Bonding between atoms. Building blocks of materials. Crystal defects and diffusion. Structural properties of materials. Functional properties of materials. Phases and microstructures.

MS1016.title: Thermodynamics Of Materials
MS1016.description:
This course introduces thermodynamics at an introductory to intermediate level.
1.	Concept of work, heat, enthalpy and entropy. Laws of thermodynamics
2.	Concept of free energy and equilibrium. Solving thermodynamic problems with Maxwell's equations. 
3.	Application of theories to single-component solutions, multi-component solutions and electrochemistry.

MS2012.title: Introduction To Manufacturing Processes
MS2012.description: Fundamentals of casting and overview of casting processes. Fundamentals of metal deformation and overview of metal deformation processes. Vacuum deposition processes. Machining and cutting of materials. Powder processing. Overview of polymer processing and electronics materials processing.

MS2013.title: Polymers And Composites
MS2013.description: Introduction to polymer; Step growth and chain growth polymerization; Structure and transitions of polymers; Viscoelastic properties, and Elementary principle of composite materials.

MS2014.title: Materials Structure And Defects
MS2014.description:
This course introduces crystallography and crystal structures at an intermediate level.

Fundamental crystallography.
Structure of metals and alloys
Defects in metals 
Ceramic structures and defects

MS2015.title: Mechanical Behaviour Of Materials
MS2015.description: Stress and strain. Elasticity and plasticity: deformation mechanisms. Strengths and failure criteria. Ductile-brittle transition. Materials strengthening. Creep deformation and failure. Fracture and fatigue.

MS2016.title: Phase Transformation And Kinetics
MS2016.description:
This course introduces theory of design in an introductory to intermediate level.

Diffusion being a mechanism of atomic and molecular change is solids will be covered in greater details following the basics taught in year one
Phase transformations and the kinetics of these transformations
Interfacial Studies
Heat Transfer

MS2018.title: Electronics & Magnetic Properties Of Materials
MS2018.description: Classical theory of metal; Introduction to quantum mechanics; Modern theory of metals; Semiconductors and semiconductor devices; Dielectric materials; Magnetism and magnetic materials.

MS2081.title: Laboratory Iia
MS2081.description: Students will perform five different laboratory experiments related to the various subjects covered in Materials Science & Engineering

MS2082.title: Laboratory Iib
MS2082.description: Students will perform five different laboratory experiments related to the various subjects covered in Materials Science & Engineering.

MS3011.title: Metallic & Ceramic Materials
MS3011.description: Introduction and classification of engineering metals and alloys. Strengthening mechanisms. Microstructure and heat treatment of ferrous alloys. Mechanical properties of ferrous alloys. Non Ferrous alloys. Engineering ceramics. Functional ceramics.

MS3012.title: Micro/Nanoelectronic Materials Processing
MS3012.description: Microelectronics Technology Overview. Semiconductor Device Physics. Bulk Crystal Growth. Diffusion and Thermal Oxidation. Ion Implantation & Simulation. Thin Film Deposition. Patterning. Advanced Lithography. Advanced Deposition Techniques. Advanced Devices

MS3013.title: Environmental Effects On Materials
MS3013.description:
This course introduces environmental effects on materials performance
Effects on metal, ceramic and polymer based materials.
Prevention of materials degradation induced by environment

MS3014.title: Analysis Of Materials
MS3014.description:
This course introduces a broad range of characterization techniques in the following areas:
1.	Chemical Analysis
2.	Spectroscopy Techniques
3.	Basic Imaging Techniques
4.	Basic Crystal Structure Analysis
5.	Physical Properties Analysis

MS3015.title: Materials Aspects In Design
MS3015.description:
This course introduces theory of design in an intermediate to advanced level.
1.	Principle of design process, motivation and translation.
2.	Develop charts to rank materials according the objective. Use charts to obtain the global overview of engineering materials and develop strategy in the design of new materials. 
3.	A 10 week group design project on materials-related topics

MS3081.title: Laboratory III
MS3081.description: Students will perform five different laboratory experiments related to the various subjects covered in Materials Science & Engineering.

MS4012.title: Quality Control
MS4012.description: Descriptive statistics; Commonly used distributions; Confidence Intervals; Hypothesis testing; Statistical process control; Acceptance sampling and data analysis; Quality costs, management and improvement.

MS4013.title: Biomaterials
MS4013.description: Introduction to Biomaterials; Biology and Medicine; Biocompatibility; Biological Testing of Materials; Classes of Materials used in Medicine; Applications

MS4014.title: Nanomaterials: Fundamentals And Applications
MS4014.description: Introduction to nanomaterials, size effects, properties and applications of nanomaterials, synthesis methods, stabilization and assembly of nanomaterials, characterization of nanomaterials, and existing & emerging applications (case studies).

MS4603.title: Microelectronics Process Integration
MS4603.description: Process integration for ULSI devices. CMOS well/isolation/gate module technology. Contact module technology. Interconnect and Metallization. Applications of Thin Films

MS4610.title: Advanced Biomaterials
MS4610.description: Advanced Medical Ceramics. Fibers and Composites. Biodegradable Materials. Smart Biomaterials. Surface Modifications of Biomaterials. Applications.

MS4620.title: Polymer Technology
MS4620.description:
This course is offered to fourth year students. It aims to introduce important additives and processing techniques commonly used in the manufacturing of thermoplastic and thermosetting polymeric products. The effects of fillers and stabilizers on properties of the polymer materials are introduced. Factors affecting polymer processing are being taught which includes basic rheology, the importance of viscoelasticity in polymers, factors affecting polymer flow and flow through die channels of various geometries. 

Polymer additives, melt rheology and polymer processes.

MS4631.title: Corrosion Engineering
MS4631.description: Corrosion in Various Materials. Nonmetallics: Ceramics, carbon and graphite, polymers and plastics. Corrosion in Various Environments. Advanced Corrosion Prevention Technologies. Corrosion Testing and Monitoring Techniques ? Destructive Testing. Corrosion Testing and Monitoring Techniques ? Non-Destructive Testing Radiography.

MS4640.title: Advanced Analysis Of Materials
MS4640.description:
This course focuses on advanced crystallographic techniques, with emphasis in the following topics:
Basics of Crystallography
Advanced X-ray Diffraction Techniques
Advanced Transmission Electron Microscopy
Integration of results for nanomaterials analysis

MS4650.title: Functional Nanostructure Materials
MS4650.description: General introduction of nanomaterials. Case studies of nanomaterial systems in term of the applications, synthesis and characterization. For example, using carbon nanotubes for electronic device applications; noble metal nanoparticles for catalysis.

MS4651.title: Thin Film Technology
MS4651.description: Thin film deposition techniques. Thin film characterization. Nucleation, growth and microstructural evolution during thin film formation. Thin film properties and application case studies.

MS4660.title: Fundamentals Of Intellectual Property In Matls Sci And Eng
MS4660.description:
This course provides students with a general overview of intellectual property (IP) and the importance of IP to the organization. Students will be able to apply their IP knowledge to support the organizational procedures and registration procedures of IP in Singapore:

1.	Definition of IP / What IP is, Types of IP 
2.	Sources from which information about IP can be obtained 
3.	Registration procedures, if any, of various types of IP in Singapore

MT1001.title: Mathematics I For Maritime Studies
MT1001.description: Function and graph. Limits and continuity. Mathematics of finance: interest, geometric series, investment appraisal. Differential. Optimization of business functions. Indefinite and definite integrations. Application of integrals in business and economics. Partial and total differentiation. Production function analysis. Double integrals. Applications of double integrals in ship technology.

MT1002.title: Introduction To Maritime Industry
MT1002.description: Facts and figures highlighting the importance of shipping to the world of trade; Brief introduction to types of ships Geographical origins and destination of major cargo; Maritime Perils, Meteorology; Role of Broker, Charterers, Shipper, Carrier, Consignee, Distributor, Retailer and end-user; Contracts of carriage, Charter parties, Shipping services; Port operations, Concepts of Maritime logistics; Basics of Shipping economics; Ship management, Quality control; Ship Operations; Ship board operations, Seaworthiness; Maritime Legal Infrastructure, Jurisdiction; Maritime Safety and Security, Marine pollution, Maritime Environmental issues.

MT1003.title: Trade Practice And Incoterms
MT1003.description: Importance of sale contract and the contract with the carrier, Inter-modal and multi-modal transports, Agreements of sale and purchase, Incoterms 2000 or latest version, Methods of Payment of freight, Characteristics and bills of lading - liability and limitations, Risk and insurance of vessels and cargo, Basic Chartering and Ship Broking Terms, Legal aspects and some commercial aspects of chartering contracts, Carriage of Goods by Sea e.g. Hague Rules, Hague/Visby Rules, Carrier's Liabilities and Limitations, Exceptions, Defences available, Burden of Proof.

MT2002.title: Shipping Economics
MT2002.description: Maritime trade and cargo. Shipping market. Market cycle. Supply and demand. Freight and cost structure. Tramp shipping. Liner shipping.

MT2003.title: Maritime Technology
MT2003.description:
Introduction to ship hydrostatics and buoyancy. Forces on plane surfaces and location of centre of buoyancy. Longitudinal and transverse stability and free surface effects. Trim.

Introduction to fictional resistance and wave making resistance. Hull strength, powering and model testing. Identifying different ship types.

MT4001.title: Shipping Logistics
MT4001.description: Key logistics activities. Total cost concept. The supply chain system. Shipping value chain. Just-in-time concept. Risk pooling. Logistical strategic partnerships. Bullwhip effect. Global logistics. Current trends in shipping logistics. Logistics arms of shipping-related companies.

MT4002.title: Essentials Of Project Management
MT4002.description: Purposes of Project Management, Project process, selection/estimating. Project organization. Project planning and scheduling. Project control and monitoring. Tools and methodology. Project closure/termination.

MT4003.title: Maritime Strategy
MT4003.description: Strategic planning and management in supply chains including shipping. Schools of thoughts of strategy, including industrial organization theories, resource-based and competencies-based views. Generic strategies and sources of competitive advantage. Organizational structure and business process improvement. Globalization and international management. Modes of expansion strategies such as partnering, alliances, mergers and acquisitions.

MT4101.title: Intermodal Transportation
MT4101.description: Concepts and operational specifics of commercial intermodal transportation pertaining to freight movement. Intermodal services, terminals, equipment and information systems. Interactions between individual modes and intermediaries. Advantages and disadvantages of intermodalism. Intermodal operations management. Business strategies for intermodal management.

MT4104.title: Information Technology Management
MT4104.description: Introduction to Technology Applications. E-Commerce and E-Business Concepts. Personal Technology Use. Enterprise Systems Technology and Infrastructure: The Wired World. Technology Convergence. Disruptive Technologies. Technical Solutions and Standards. Building E-commerce Solutions. Managing Business Value of Information Technology and E-commerce. E-commerce and Consumer Behavior. E-commerce and Technology Use. Ethical, Social and Political Issues. Testing and Evaluating E-commerce Solutions.

PH1104.title: Mechanics
prerequisite: Maths at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH1104.description:
This course introduces fundamental concepts of mechanics.

Fundamental quantities of nature. Systems in equilibrium, in motion with constant acceleration and non-constant acceleration. Frames of reference and Galilean Relativity.

Linear Motion - Newton's three laws of motion; forces, linear momentum, impulse, work done, kinetic energy, potential energy, torque and pressure; conservation laws; collisions; systems with variable masses; rockets. Force fields - gravitation; concept of field; conservative fields; Gauss' law; superposition.

Rotational motion - Orbits & Kepler's laws; angular speed and momentum; moment of inertia; rotational dynamics; parallel and perpendicular axes theorems; kinetic energy; gyroscope;

PH1105.title: Optics, Vibrations And Waves
prerequisite: Maths at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH1105.description:
This course studies the behaviour and properties of optical and particle waves.

Geometrical Optics - reflection, refraction and dispersion; lensmaker's equation; real and virtual images; cameras, telescope and microscope.

Oscillations - Simple Harmonic Motion; relative phases; pendulums; damped and driven oscillations; phasor diagrams.

Waves and Sound - Wave equation, characteristics of waves; wave attenuation; phase, group velocity; Huygen's principle, superposition and interference; Sound waves and characteristics; beats; standing waves; Doppler effect.

Wave Optics - electromagnetic waves; interference, diffraction; Young's slits and diffraction grating; Limits of resolution; Interference in thin films; Scattering of light; Michelson's interferometer; Spectrometer, X-ray diffraction, Bragg?s equation; Polarization; Brewster angle.

PH114S.title: Mechanics*^
prerequisite: Maths at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH114S.description:
This course introduces fundamental concepts of mechanics.

Fundamental quantities of nature. Systems in equilibrium, in motion with constant acceleration and non-constant acceleration. Frames of reference and Galilean Relativity.

Linear Motion - Newton's three laws of motion; forces, linear momentum, impulse, work done, kinetic energy, potential energy, torque and pressure; conservation laws; collisions; systems with variable masses; rockets. Force fields - gravitation; concept of field; conservative fields; Gauss' law; superposition.

Rotational motion - Orbits & Kepler's laws; angular speed and momentum; moment of inertia; rotational dynamics; parallel and perpendicular axes theorems; kinetic energy; gyroscope;

PH115S.title: Optics, Vibrations And Waves*^
prerequisite: Maths at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH115S.description:
This course studies the behaviour and properties of optical and particle waves.

Geometrical Optics - reflection, refraction and dispersion; lensmaker's equation; real and virtual images; cameras, telescope and microscope.

Oscillations - Simple Harmonic Motion; relative phases; pendulums; damped and driven oscillations; phasor diagrams.

Waves and Sound - Wave equation, characteristics of waves; wave attenuation; phase, group velocity; Huygen's principle, superposition and interference; Sound waves and characteristics; beats; standing waves; Doppler effect.

Wave Optics - electromagnetic waves; interference, diffraction; Young's slits and diffraction grating; Limits of resolution; Interference in thin films; Scattering of light; Michelson's interferometer; Spectrometer, X-ray diffraction, Bragg?s equation; Polarization; Brewster angle.

PH116S.title: Electricity And Magnetism^
prerequisite: Physics and Mathematics at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH116S.description:
This course introduces basic notions of Electric, Magnetic fields and circuits.

Electric fields - Coulomb?s law, electric field & potential; Gauss? law; capacitors and capacitance; Current of electricity; Ohm?s Law; Microscopic model of electrical conduction. Kirchoff?s laws; RC circuits.

Magnetic fields ? Biot-Savart?s Law and Ampere?s law; Lorentz force; Hall effect; mass spectrometer; JJ Thompson?s experiment; magnetic flux; Gauss?s Law of magnetism; Faraday?s and Lenz?s law; transformers; inductors and inductance.

Electrical circuits - voltage, current and resistance; Oscillations in circuits - LC circuits and relative phases; complex current and voltage; complex impedance; LCR circuits and electrical resonance. High pass filters and low pass filters.

Electromagnetic Waves ? properties of electromagnetic waves; Poynting vector.

PH117S.title: Relativity And Quantum Physics*^
prerequisite: Physics and Mathematics at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH117S.description:
This course introduces fundamental concepts of special relativity, quantum physics and some basic applications.

Special Relativity - Michelson-Morley experiment; Einstein's postulates; time and causality; Lorentz transformation; world-lines & space-time diagrams; Doppler effect; relativistic momentum and energy; mass energy equivalence.

Quantum Physics - Planck's postulate; Photoelectric effect; photons; Compton scattering; wave particle duality; electron diffraction; de Broglie waves; Bohr's atom and its limitations; Schrodinger's Equation; Born's interpretation of wave functions; Uncertainty Principle; Infinite square well; Tunneling; Schrodinger's analysis of hydrogen atom; Wave functions of Hydrogen Atom; Atomic structure; Electron spin; Quantum numbers; Pauli's Exclusion principle; Many-electron atoms; Photomultipliers; scanning electron microscope; scanning tunneling microscope;

Nuclear Physics and Radioactivity - radioactive decay; binding energy; activities and half- lives; fission and fusion; radiation doses.

PH1198.title: Physics Laboratory Ia
prerequisite: Physics at A or H2 level or equivalent.
PH1198.description: This course will train students in basic experimental physics that include topics in mechanics, basic optics and thermal physics. The laboratory sessions are designed to provide an active learning experience where key concepts can be better appreciated. Students will also learn about data acquisition, error analysis, error distribution and fitting procedures.

PH1801.title: Foundations Of Physics I
prerequisite: Physics and Mathematics at A or H2 level or equivalent
PH1801.description:
Foundations of physics covering (a) mechanics, (b) wave motion, and (c) thermodynamics, with examples of practical applications to biomedical sciences, engineering sciences and other fields. 
Students learn about the principles of the physical world from which scientific and engineering applications are built upon. At a general level, students learn how to read scientific material effectively, identify fundamental concepts, reason through scientific questions, and solve quantitative problems. This course is Pass/Fail graded.

PH2103.title: Thermal Physics
PH2103.description:
This course introduces the laws and key concepts of thermodynamics.
Thermodynamic equilibrium, functions of state, equations of state. Zeroth law. 
Perfect gases and absolute zero. First law of thermodynamics. Work, heat and internal energy. Adiabatic, reversible and irreversible changes. Heat engines, efficiency and Carnot cycles. 
Clausius? theorem and Second law of thermodynamics. Fundamental equation of thermodynamics. Phase changes and latent heat. Enthalpy, Helmholtz free energy and Gibb?s energy. Maxwell relations. Reciprocity theorem. Third law of thermodynamics. 
Kinetic theory - Maxwell distribution of velocities; pressure and effusion; mean free path; thermal conductivity and viscosity. Heat transport - conduction, radiation and convection as transport mechanisms; heat flux and heat diffusion equation; steady-state and initial-value problems; sinusoidally varying surface temperatures.

PH2104.title: Analytical Mechanics
PH2104.description:
This course introduces fundamental concepts of analytical mechanics. 

Newtonian Mechanics: Motion with non-constant acceleration; Potential energy and conservative force; Conservative forces in three dimensions; Small oscillations; Coupled oscillators; Central forces; Orbits and Trajectories; Scattering. Collision in center of mass coordinates.

Rotating Systems: Rotating coordinate systems; Coriolis forces and Centrifugal forces; Focault Pendulum; Rigid body rotation; inertia tensor, principal axes of inertia, precession. 

Lagrangian mechanics: calculus of variations; action integral; Hamilton?s principle of least action; generalised coordinates; Hamilton?s equations; Canonical transformations; Liouville?s theorem; Symmetries and conservation laws.

PH2198.title: Physics Laboratory Iia
PH2198.description: This course will train students in experimental physics covering a wide variety of topics: Electromagnetism, thermal physics, solid state and materials physics.

PH3101.title: Quantum Mechanics II
PH3101.description:
This course introduces the framework and basic tenets of quantum mechanics.

?	Review of introductory quantum mechanics: wavefunction and uncertainty principle, Schrodinger equation, one-dimensional examples (square well, harmonic oscillator, periodic potential)

?	Formalism of quantum mechanics: state of a system, dynamical variables and operators, expansions in eigenfunctions, commutation, unitary transformations, matrix representations, time evolution, Schrodinger and Heisenberg pictures, path integrals, symmetry principles and conservation laws, the classical limit.

?	Angular momentum: orbital angular momentum and spatial rotations, eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, particle on a sphere and rigid rotator, general angular momentum, matrix representations, spin and total angular momentum, addition of angular momentum.

?	Schrodinger equation in 3 dimensions: separation of variables, central potentials, free particle, 3-D square well, hydrogenic atoms, 3-D isotropic oscillator.

?	Approximation methods: Time-independent perturbation theory for non-degenerate and degenerate levels, variational method, WKB approximation, time-dependent perturbation theory.

PH3102.title: Condensed Matter Physics I
PH3102.description:
This course introduces the structure of solids and the quantization of atomic and electronic motion in a periodic solid.
Crystal symmetry - lattice, basis, unit cell, Miller indices, lattice planes and spacing; reciprocal lattice and Brillouin zones. Bragg and Laue diffraction, structure factor, atomic form factor; neutron and x-ray diffraction; powder and single crystal diffraction.
Normal mode dispersion for linear atomic chains; acoustic and optic modes; Born von Karman boundary conditions; density of states; lattice quantization and phonons; Einstein and Debye models of heat capacity.
Free electron theory, density of states, Fermi energy, Fermi surface.
Metals - conductivity and heat capacity; density of states at Fermi level; nearly free electron model and band gaps. Bloch theorem, Kronig-Penny model.
Distinction between metals, semiconductors and insulators. Aspects of Condensed Matter Physics.

PH3199.title: Physics Lab Iiia
PH3199.description: This course provides advanced training in experimental physics covering a wide a variety of topics: Quantum physics, electrodynamics, atomic physics and spectroscopy, solid state physics, fluid mechanics, semiconductor physics, photonics, biophysics, vacuum technology and thin film growth.

PH3501.title: Fluid Mechanics
PH3501.notAvailableToProgramme: AERO, CEE, CVEC, ENE, ENEC, ENG, ME, ME(DES), ME(MEC), MS
PH3501.description:
This course introduces the laws governing fluid motion. 
Pascal?s theorem, Bernoulli equation, Euler?s equation, Navier-Stokes equation. Vorticity and divergence. 
Compressible and incompressible fluids, flow around objects, potential flow. Viscosity, Reynolds number. Laminar flow and turbulence. Kolmogorov scaling.
Sound waves. Shock fronts, Rankine-Hugoniot relations. 
Hydrostatic balance, shallow-water equations, surface waves. Conservation of potential vorticity.

PH3601.title: Fabrication Of Micro-And Nanoelectronic Devices
PH3601.description:
This course discusses the basic principles underlying the fabrication of micro- and nanoelectronic devices and material processing techniques.
Semiconductor based device fabrication - ion implantation, diffusion, oxidation, epitaxy, thin film deposition, material and device characterization, lithography, etching and cleaning. 
Conventional and non-conventional fabrication techniques of magnetic, organic and bioMEMS devices, and its characterization techniques will be discussed.

PH3602.title: Photonics
PH3602.description:
This course introduces key concepts in optical, optoelectronics and optical communication technologies.
Waveguides optics, fiber optics, crystal optics, interaction between photons and semiconductors, semiconductor light sources and detectors, photovoltaic devices, liquid crystal optics, and flat panel displays.

PH4402.title: Condensed Matter Physics II
PH4402.description:
This course introduces advanced concepts in solid state physics with particular attention to theoretical approaches.
Transport and scattering - crystal momentum; neutron scattering; electron-phonon scattering; optical conductivity; Drude theory, plasmons; transport in electric and magnetic fields; quantization of orbits, cyclotron resonance; de Haas-van Alphen effect; Fermi surfaces; magnetoresistance oscillation
Semiconductors - thermal equilibrium of quaisparticles; field effect transistor; pn junctions, LED; exciton, heterostrutures, quantum well, semiconductor laser.
Magnetism - origin moments and interactions. ferromagnetism; itinerant magnetism, Stoner model;.strongly intercting systems, Mott insulator.
Superconductor ? Phenomenology of Superconductivity, Microscopic theory of superconductivity

PH4403.title: Surfaces And Interfaces
PH4403.description:
This course discusses the key concepts in surface and interface science with special focus on electronic structure.
Surface energy and thermodynamics; electronic structure; phase transition; elementary excitations; physisorption and chemisorption; energy transfer.
Schottky barrier and band offsets in semiconductors; band engineering.
Analytical techniques include scanning tunneling microscopy; electron diffraction methods; photoemission

PH4408.title: Nuclear Physics
PH4408.description:
This course provides a basic understanding of the structure of nuclei and their properties.
Properties of nuclei: radii, masses, abundances, binding energies, spins and EM moments
Nuclear structure: deuteron, nucleon-nucleon scattering in terms of an exchange force. Nuclear models: the semi-empirical mass formula, the Fermi gas model, the shell model, liquid drop model with vibrational and rotational excitations, collective structure
Energy balances and spin/parity selection rules of alpha, beta and gamma decay processes
Measurement of nuclear lifetimes, applications of nuclear physics including fusion and fission processes. Nuclear reactors and nuclear power; neutron diffusion and moderation; radiation protection and radiation shielding; safety & the environment.

PH4411.title: Introduction To Experimental Particle Physics
prerequisite: Approved by Division of Physics and Applied Physics
PH4411.description:
This course is a survey of particle physics for advanced undergraduate and beginning graduate students. It explores the common roots and tools of the nuclear (medium energy) and particle (high energy) fields. The main objective is to develop an understanding of the Standard Model of quarks, leptons and the fundamental interactions of the universe together with the associated experimental techniques.
Specific topics include an introduction to the fundamental interactions and their mediators, quarks and leptons, symmetries and tests of conservation laws, and indications of physics beyond the Standard Model. The course in particular includes experimental techniques in particle physics, including the physics principles of particle accelerators and particle detectors. The lectures on particle accelerators will include selected topics in the types of accelerators, transverse & longitudinal dynamics, the lattice, magnets, RF and plasma acceleration, as well as electron dynamics & synchrotron radiation. The particle detector lectures will include a presentation of the main properties of particle interactions with matter, which form the basis of all particle detectors. The various types of detectors used in particle physics experiments are discussed in detail, including their sensitivity, detector response, energy, space and time resolution response functions, detector efficiency and dead time, covering devices for position and momentum measurements, particle identification systems, calorimeters and multipurpose systems, as well as the overall design of a particle physics experiment. Current and future experimental challenges will be discussed for modern particle physics experiments, including the data volume and computing challenge, the online collision selection, and the data analyses - taking the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments at CERN as an example. . 
The application of such accelerators and detectors, for example in the medical and industrial sectors, will be discussed as well.

PH4501.title: Statistical Mechanics II
PH4501.description:
This course introduces the theoretical framework of statistical mechanics and applications to novel physical systems.
?	Principle of detailed balance; Principle of equal a priori probability; microcanonical, canonical and grand canonical ensembles; Boltzmann and Gibbs entropy; fluctuations in energy, particle number and volume; configurational entropy and defects; classical statistical mechanics.

?	Ideal systems: Ideal classical gas; non-interacting fermions and bosons; paramagnetism (classical and quantum treatment); harmonic oscillator; blackbody radiation; equipartition of energy; negative temperature; critical opalescence.

?	Interacting systems 1: Virial expansion; van der Waals equation of state.

?	Interacting systems 2: Mean-field approximation; nematic crystals; adsorption; Monte Carlo method; Ising model; spin-1/2 paramagnet; Landau mean-field theory

?	Interacting systems 3: Critical phenomenon; critical exponents

PH4507.title: Topics In Physics
PH4507.description: This course introduces students to topics in Physics which are at the frontier of theoretical physics. Topics are chosen from various areas of theoretical physics, such as general relativity, quantum field theory, elementary particle physics, quantum chromodynamics, astrophysics, cosmology, string theory, condensed matter physics etc. Students will be informed of the topic selected before the start of the semester

PH4604.title: Topics In Applied Physics
PH4604.description: This course introduces students to topics in Physics which are at the frontier of applied physics. Topics are chosen from various areas of applied physics, such as advanced material physics, spintronics, physics of organic devices, nanophysics, superconductivity and its application etc. Students will be informed of the topic selected before the start of the semester.

RE1001.title: Mathematics I
RE1001.description: Mathematics I serves as an introductory course for all Renaissance students in Year 1. This course covers topics in basic mathematics with emphasis on real valued functions of a real variable. Limits of such functions, continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem. Differentiability, chain rule, critical points, the Mean Value Theorem. Inverse functions and derivatives of inverse functions. Integrability and integrals. Fundamental Theorems of Calculus. Trigonometric, logarithm and exponential functions. Techniques of integration. Taylor?s formula. Infinite sequences. Infinite series. Power series and radius of convergence. Ordinary Differential Equations and techniques for solving such. Through the sample questions/exercises provided in the course material, the students will have chances to pick up the fundamental principles related concepts into engineering science applications.

RE1004.title: Engineering Science I
RE1004.description: Engineering Science I serves as an introductory course for all Renaissance students in year 1. This course covers topics in basic mathematics with emphasis on first- and second-order ordinary differential equations, basic physics with emphasis on electricity, magnetism, light and optics, and basic chemistry with more advanced discussions on the fundamental concepts and materials used in the earth, sustainability, life and natural cycles and environmental related problems. Through the sample questions/exercises provided in the course material, the students will have chances to pick up the fundamental principles related concepts into engineering science applications.

RE1005.title: Introductory Thermal Sciences And Electricity
RE1005.description: The first part of this course aims to provide students with an understanding of the basic principles of electric power and machines. It covers the fundamentals of power systems, electromagnetism, transformers and rotating machines. The second part of this course aims to provide students with a good understanding of the fundamental principles of thermal-fluids sciences. It covers topics on fluid mechanics, temperature and ideal gases, laws of thermodynamics and mechanisms of heat and mass transfer. Applications of these concepts in solving simple engineering problems will also be covered.

RE1006.title: Materials And Manufacturing Engineering
RE1006.description:
This course provides an essential foundation to subsequent courses in the curriculum. As well as providing fundamental description of the underlying material science concepts, it enables the student to appreciate how these factors relate to the development of mechanical properties, functional properties, as well as manufacturing processes. A pivotal objective in the course is environmental awareness and responsibility for material choice. 
Both the materials and manufacturing factors are drawn together by a thematic study of the i-PAD, as well as a hands-on session in a semiconductor laboratory.

RE2002.title: Electronic And Information Engineering II
RE2002.description: The first part of this course provides an introduction to the laws of electromagnetism including static and time-varying electric and magnetic fields, Maxwell's equations, uniform plane waves, electromagnetic energy transfer, reflection and transmission of electromagnetic wave and transmission lines. In the second part, students will learn about control and information systems engineering. The topics covered are: fundamentals of control systems, system modelling, time domain analysis, performance of feedback control systems, frequency domain analysis, computer control systems, computer communications and data communications fundamentals.

RE2003.title: Mechanical & Structural Engineering II
RE2003.description:
The purpose of a mechanism is to transmit motion and force. This course introduces the students some basic mechanisms including linkages, cams and gears. Mechanisms are the building blocks of a machine. In a machine design problem, very often the first task is to determine the type and configurations of mechanisms to provide the desired motions. Once the kinematic issues are addressed, the dynamic analysis can then be performed. In this course, techniques for the kinematic and dynamic analyses of mechanisms will be covered. A course in the theory of mechanisms is essential for any mechanical engineer as the knowledge is fundamental in understanding the working of machines. Apart from analytical ability, it also provides students the opportunities to develop their design capability.

On structural analysis of trusses, beams and frames, the course covers the determination of deflection curve using the energy methods and principle of virtual work.

On vibration of structural systems, it covers the equations of motion of single degree and multiple degrees of freedom systems, effects of damping, and the structural response to ground excitations.

RE2005.title: Engineering Science II
RE2005.description: Engineering Science II serves as an introductory course for all Renaissance students in year 2. It aims to equip students with a firm foundation and superior problem-solving skills in the science of chemistry and biology. As an introductory course, it exposes the student to a wide spectrum of technical concepts. The topics include: redox processes, electrochemistry, energy storage, transition metal chemistry of metal complexes, spectroscopy analytical chemistry , cell growth kinetics, bioreactor design, and bioprocess engineering, biomechanics, molecular recognition, systems physiology, spectroscopy and pharmacokinetics. Student will also be introduced to the relevant fundamentals of energy, biology and medicine, including applications such as fuel cells, regenerative medicine, biosensors and artificial organ devices.

RE2006.title: Engineering Computation
RE2006.description:
This course aims at developing students? understanding of the CPU of a computer, how it functions and how to program a computer in order to solve problems. Students are introduced to the hardware architecture of the CPU, the timing of different types of signals that control the functioning of the CPU. They are taught how to program a CPU using assembly language that resembles very closely the codes that are executed by the CPU. They learn how to connect different peripheral devices so that the CPU can interact with the external world. Different types of memories and how to interface them are also introduced.

Further, this course also aims to develop students? understanding of the fundamental concepts, implementations and applications associated with data structures in computing such as arrays, stacks, queues and linked lists and to use such data structures to solve real world problems. Abstract data types and dynamic memory allocation will also be covered.

SP0003.title: The Great Ideas
prerequisite: Only for University Scholars Programme (USP) students.
SP0003.description: This course is about great ideas. 'Great ideas' in this context refers to those ideas that have had a significant and enduring impact on academic, artistic, political, socioeconomic, and scientific developments in our time or that they shine new light on conventions and cause a paradigm shift in sensibility and thought. They are ideas that have had a notable influence on how people think of themselves, of other people, and about the world. They are ideas that provoke hearty endorsement. They are also ideas that incite vehement objection. The works explored in this course are only part of what can be considered a canon of ideas that have been produced by generations of remarkable activists, intellectuals, philosophers, and scientists who, echoing Socrates, considered the unexamined life not worth living. It is hoped nonetheless that these albeit limited number of ideas will at the least convey the excitement of intellectual pursuits, and move readers of this course to critically reflect on their lives and times. Organizationally, the course will explore ideas hailing from a wide array of disciplines. Depending on the course instructor, new themes and readings may be included for discussion.

SP0004.title: Es Planet Earth
prerequisite: Only for University Scholars Programme (USP) students.
SP0004.description: This course examines the Earth and its systems through lecture, group-based inquiry learning, and individual reading, writing, and research. Content is based on major discoveries by scientists in the broad fields of Astronomy, Geosciences, Geography, and Biosciences. This will provide the gateway for investigation into such topics as the formation of the solar system, the lithosphere, the atmosphere, and climate change, ocean circulation, the biosphere, ecology, and how humans interact with the environment.

SS1001.title: Structural & Functional Anatomy
SS1001.description: This module deals with the various systems of the human body and the part each system plays in human movement. The aim of this module is also to enable participants to relate the structures and functions of the human body to physical performance, health and fitness. This module will also lay the foundation for further work in Exercise & Sports Physiology, Biomechanics and other disciplines in sport science. The mode of delivery of this module will be in the form of Lectures and Laboratories.

SS1002.title: Sociology Of Sport I
SS1002.description: The course focuses on cultural elements of the development of sport and physical activity in society today. The antecedents of today?s sport and physical activity patterns are examined in relation to changes in value systems that have occurred with the passage of time. Ranging from the origins of the Olympic Movement in Ancient Greece to the spread of a colonial model by the British, this course provides a foundation for sport studies of systems in many countries.

SS1003.title: Introduction To Sport Management
SS1003.description: The course provides students of basic introductions in the field of sport management. Definitions and disciplinary foundations of sport management will be presented. Basic concepts of sub-disciplines in sport management will be introduced.

SS2002.title: Motor Learning & Control 1
SS2002.description: This module is designed to provide students with background knowledge in motor skill acquisition. Emphasis is on the theoretical and practical nature of motor skill acquisition and retention in relation to motor-physical performances.

SS2003.title: Sport Biomechanics 1
SS2003.description: Biomechanics is the study of a biological system by means of mechanics. This module introduces the basic mechanical concepts and principles that govern human movement. The aim of this module is to enable participants to perform qualitative analyses of human movement using basic concepts of mechanics and anatomy. Basic quantitative analysis will also be introduced to allow participants to evaluate numerically the nature of the movement.

SS2004.title: Coaching & Learning 1
SS2004.description: This course examines and applies practical sport coach pedagogy (learning theories and instructional models) to the sport environment. The course also considers pedagogical knowledge and application of the principles of motor skills' learning.

SS2005.title: Physical Activity & Leisure For Special Populations
SS2005.description: THIS MODULE ADDRESSES PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES AND RELATED TOPICS TO IMPROVE FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY IN SPECIAL POPULATION INCLUDING VARIOUS CHRONIC DISEASE PATIENTS AND THE ELDERLY. PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL FEATURES OF CHRONIC DISEASES AND PRECAUTIONS AND GUIDELINES FOR EXERCISE WILL BE ADDRESSED.

SS3001.title: Statistics, Measurement & Evaluation
SS3001.description: This course is designed to provide students with basic concepts of measurement and evaluation in sport science and management. In addition, the course will focus on fundamental concepts of statistics and the use of computers for data analysis. Accordingly, the module introduces students to measurement issues in the sport science and management contexts, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, the research process, the method of science, scientific investigation, the definition and evaluation of a research problem, hypothesis formation, and data collection.

SS3101.title: Exercise & Sport Physiology II
SS3101.description: A lecture/demonstration laboratory course is designed for the study of selected topics of exercise physiology. The principles of nutrition applied to sports performance and exercise will also be included. Emphasis will be placed on energy release and substrate utilization, energy metabolism during exercise, fluid intake and athletic performance, ergogenic aids, vitamins and minerals, the pre-game meal, sports anemia, nutritional considerations for the diabetic individual, lipid metabolism and coronary heart disease.

SS3103.title: Sports Injuries II
SS3103.description: Physical activity is associated with multiple health benefits and enhanced quality of life. Sports participation across populations in the society is on the rise. Moreover, there has been a significant increase in number of adventure sports participants in recent times. The injury risks, patterns, principles of management and preventive strategies are different in each cohort. This course is designed to provide students with knowledge and the understanding of population-specific sports injuries and skills for primary management of injuries and preventive strategies.

SS3201.title: Sport Biomechanics II
SS3201.description: This course introduces participants to quantitative methods for determining mechanical parameters of movement, namely linear and angular kinematics and kinetics. Through laboratory work, participants will also learn about the operation of the equipment associated with the measuring techniques in sports biomechanics. Participants will be introduced to the theory governing these measurement techniques and studies that use of these measurement techniques. The aim of the course is to enable participants to effectively analyse movement, explain causes of observed effects and to correct errors in physical performance in sports through the use of these quantitative methods. Participants should have completed the mechanical and anatomical bases of human motion before enrolling for this course.

SS3301.title: Exercise & Sport Psychology II
SS3301.description: This focus of this module is on psychology of sport and physical activity. The module is designed to provide students with an understanding of how psychological variables influence participation in sport and physical activity. The main focus is on the key motivational perspectives of exercise and sport but advance topics such as children in sport, burnout, psychology of injury and exercise psychology will also be covered.

SS3303.title: Coaching & Learning II
SS3303.description: This course following on the work undertaken in Coaching & Learning - Foundation 1 examines and applies practical sport coach pedagogy (learning theories and instructional models) to the sport environment. The course also considers pedagogical knowledge and application of the principles of motor skills? learning. This compulsory course critically examines and applies sport coach pedagogy (learning theories, preferences and instructional models as it relates to movement) to the sport environment.

SS3401.title: Motor Learning & Control II
SS3401.description: This course addresses behavioural aspects of human movement. Interpreting and intervening human performances from the psychomotor domain are the main foci of this course. Topics to be covered include practice conditions, feedback and skill acquisition, theories of motor learning, and measurements of motor performances.

SS3601.title: Sport Marketing & Sponsorship
SS3601.description: The course on sport marketing and sponsorship investigates the nature of sport products and the motivations of sport consumers. The sport consumer types are identified and their behaviour discussed. The essentials of marketing will be taught and related to sport. Students of the course will be given opportunity to work on a sport marketing project to appreciate and reinforce the complexity and dynamics of sport marketing. Sponsorship issues and strategies will also be covered including the relationship of sponsors to the sport, platforms and benefits of sport sponsorships.

SS3602.title: Event & Facilities Management
SS3602.description: Sport is often presented through events which can be major meets like the World Cup or Olympics or regional and local events like a school meet. Students will through this course understand the importance of sport events and the decision making considerations of hosting an event. Opportunities will also be provided for students to experientially learn event management. Important to any sport event are the sport facilities which require strict compliance to specifications and maintenance. The concept of a multi-functional sport facility will also be explored. Risk management during events and in facilities management will be highlighted.

SS3603.title: Human Resource Management In Sport
SS3603.description: Managing human resources well is vital to any organisation. Students of this course will first begin to understand the different functions of human resource management such as recruiting, inducting, developing, and assessing personnel of the organisation. An important human resource asset to most sport organisation are volunteers. The motivation to participate in sport and the strategies of retaining sport volunteers will also be discussed and explored.

SS3604.title: Legal Aspects In Sport
SS3604.description: Managing sport requires developing relationships between organisations, and between individuals representing the sport and organisation. Students of sport management must have an understanding of the legal aspects of these relationships and the roles and responsibilities of sport officials. Topics of this course include sources of law, duty of care of sport officials, the concept of tort and negligence, contracts, and others. Sport tribunals and its conduct will also be covered. Relevant case studies will be used for discussion and learning.

SS9001.title: Conditioning For Physical Fitness
SS9001.description:
Knowledge of aspects related to physical conditioning and weight training will be essential for students who plan to work in the 
fitness industry. The practical course on conditioning for physical fitness will equip our students with theoretical and practical skills to meet the needs of potential clients in fitness gyms and resorts. The course is 36 hours' duration.

SS9002.title: Principles Of Strength Training
SS9002.description:
This module is structured to provide a concept and practice-based understanding of muscular fitness and conditioning on the following aspects:

1.	Components of muscular fitness
2.	Principles of muscular exercise and fitness
a.	Muscular exercise & fitness for health and sports performance
b.	Principles of strength training and muscular fitness 
3.	Muscular fitness training
a.	Types of resistance/strength training
b.	Familiarisation to equipment for strength training
c.	Strength training programmes
d.	Designing a personal muscular fitness programme
e.	Posture and lower back strength
f.	Exercise safety and injury prevention
4.	Monitoring and assessment of muscular fitness

SS9003.title: Introduction To Pilates Matwork And Hatha Yoga
SS9003.description:
This course is structured to provide students with a good understanding of pilates matwork
and hatha yoga. Pilates Matwork will be taught in the first half of the session and followed by hatha yoga. They will get to experience the benefits of the two systems and know the differences: -

-	Pilates Matwork
Pilates is a system of physical and mental conditioning that can enhance your physical
strength, flexibility, and coordination as well as reduce stress, improve mental focus and
foster and improved sense of well-being.

-	Hatha Yoga
With it?s unique blend of physical exercises and philosophy, it can help you to bring your
body and mind into better balance. One pose, many benefits. Asana works on many body
systems simultaneously.

?	Learning the history of pilates and hatha yoga
?	Principles of pilates and philosophy of hatha yoga
?	Benefits of the pilates movements and yoga poses
?	Techniques of breathing and injury prevention
?	Understanding the sequence of pilates exercises and yoga poses
?	Strengthening and relaxing effects

SS9004.title: Track And Field
SS9004.description: This course aims to provide NTU students with the basic sports science knowledge and skills of running, jumping and throwing so as to execute and appreciate Track & Field events. Based on a systematic and hands-on approach to this course, the students will have an enjoyable time learning how to execute events such as long jump, hurdles, sprints, high jump, javelin and discus throw. This course includes the principles of training and five core bio-motor abilities so as to equip the students with the fundamental skills and knowledge to design his/her own training program.

SS9101.title: Badminton
SS9101.description: The course aims to provide students with opportunities to acquire the knowledge, understanding and experience necessary to develop an appreciation of, and play, the sport of badminton. Students will be taught the essential skills necessary to play the sport.

SS9102.title: Tennis
SS9102.description: This 36-hour course aims to impart the knowledge and competencies essential to having an informed understanding and appreciation of tennis. Students will be introduced to the basic skills necessary to play the game.

SS9103.title: Squash
SS9103.description: This course is designed to impart basic squash skills and knowledge of the game of squash to players at an introductory stage leading into intermediate levels. The emphasis of the course is on providing ample opportunities to play the game at a recreational as well as a competitive level. Also under consideration are the respective roles of player, referee and coach in creating a meaningful experience.

SS9104.title: Basketball
SS9104.description: This course is designed to provide students with the basic skills and knowledge to play and enjoy recreational basketball. Students will be taught on basic fundamental skills, rule/terminology, officiating, team offense/defense, and situational strategies.

SS9105.title: Volleyball
SS9105.description:
1.	To provide knowledge, understanding, and appreciation to the game of volleyball.
2.	To develop satisfactory competency in basic skills such as body posture, forearm pass, serve and serve reception, overhead pass, attack, block, and game situational strategies. 
3.	To provide contents and methods required to teach volleyball at an introductory level. 
4.	To provide experience in game situations and officiating the game.
5.	To be familiar with offensive and defensive strategies and able to execute them in game situations
6.	To provide understanding of the teaching/coaching techniques 
7.	To lay a foundation for more advanced study/coaching in volleyball.

SS9106.title: Netball
SS9106.description: The course is designed to impart basic netball skills and knowledge. Participants will be given the opportunity to develop the basic footwork and ball skills, goal shooting skills, and study the principles of attacking/defending, as well as the application of these skills and game concepts/tactics in game play.

SS9107.title: Table Tennis
SS9107.description:
?	Introduction to the history, rules, and current trends in table tennis
?	Concepts of grips, various racket surface(rubbers) and footwork 
?	Essential technical skills of table tennis - forehand and backhand drives, push, chops and service of various spins (top spin, under spin and side spin)
?	Specialty shots and styles of play
?	Singles and doubles strategies
?	Different competition formats
?	Use of software and video

SS9202.title: Soccer
SS9202.description: The 36-hour course aims to develop basic skills in soccer, and to provide an understanding and appreciation of the sport through an experiential process. Students will be introduced to the historical development and current trends in soccer, the technical aspects of soccer, strategies and tactics employed in the sport, and competition formats.

SS9203.title: Hockey
SS9203.description: Hockey as a game may seem ?strange and unfamiliar ?but actually it has many similarities to other sports. This course will enable students to learn the game of hockey in a fun manner. It pays particular attention to safety and will enable participants to enjoy the skills in a simple yet enjoyable manner. By the end of the course participants will be more aware of field hockey as a sport which can be enjoyed by all ages and all levels of ability.

SS9204.title: Floorball
SS9204.description: Floorball is a young and fast growing game in Singapore and the world. The game is adapted from Ice Hockey. The game has grown quickly in Singapore as it is fast paced (high intensity), safe (using plastic based equipment) and easy to pick up. This course will enable students to learn the game of floorball in a fun and safe environment through a game centered approach. By the end of the course, the students will be able to appreciate and enjoy playing the game.

SS9205.title: Rugby
SS9205.description: This course aims to develop knowledge, understanding and playing competency in the various forms of rugby football namely, tag rugby, touch rugby and contact rugby. The basic techniques, tactics and strategies will be learnt and applied in practice and match situations and analysed from theoretical, practical and biomechanical perspectives.

SS9206.title: Tchoukball
SS9206.description:
1.	To provide knowledge, understanding, and appreciation to the game of tchoukball. 
2.	To develop satisfactory competency in basic skills such as passing, receiving passes, overarm and underarm shot, catching, individual and team defence, and game situational tactics. 
3.	To provide contents and methods required to teach tchoukball at an introductory level. 
4.	To provide experience in game situations and officiating a tchoukball game. 
5.	To be familiar with offensive and defensive strategies and able to execute them in game situations 
6.	To provide understanding of the teaching/coaching techniques 
7.	To lay a foundation for more advanced studying/coaching in tchoukball.

SS9302.title: Dancesport
SS9302.description: This course is structured to provide a concept (understanding different dance elements and terminology) and practice-based understanding of dance, specifically jazz and dance sport. Basic movement activities including locomotor movements, use of space, use of dynamics and original dance patterns. Social dances include Samba, Waltz and Cha-cha.

SS9303.title: Introduction To Hip-Hop And Its Dances
SS9303.description: How many times have you wondered- what exactly is Hip-Hop? Over this course, learners will be exposed to how the Hip-Hop culture we know of today, born in the mid-1970s in an impoverished section of New York City, found its way to the mass media and mainstream population and evolved into a multi-million dollar industry. Emphasis will be placed on learning about roots of Hip-Hop, particularly its dances. Participants will learn to dance to the rhythm of music and be introduced to some common moves popularized by prominent dance pioneers.

SS9304.title: Introduction To Modern Jazz Dance
SS9304.description:
This course is structured to provide a concept and practice-based understanding of dance, specifically jazz. Together with theoretical and historical learning, participants will perform, respond and create. Movement activities include technique-based movements, locomotor movements, use of space and dynamics, and composition of dances. 

1.	Understanding the evolution of jazz dances and its historical contexts
2.	Learning dance terminology and techniques
3.	Improvising and creating dances
4.	Appreciate dances by analyzing the forms and patterns 
5.	Understanding your body through dance
6.	Create and perform dances individually and as a group

SS9401.title: Aquatics
prerequisite: No injuries/med cond100m recogn stroke nonstop/tread1.8 1min
SS9401.description:
The course aims to develop stroke competencies and techniques in swimming. Participants will be expected to practice, acquire and finally, demonstrate correct and efficient technique in a least three out of the four swimming strokes (frontcrawl, breaststroke, backstroke and butterfly).

Related activities will also be introduced in the course:
	Basic Personal Survival and Life Saving Techniques
	Fundamentals of Water Polo
	Canoe Polo Basics
	Organising Swimming / Water Sports Events

SS9402.title: Introductory Swimming
prerequisite: No skills in basic swimming.Cannot read if passed SS9401
SS9402.description:
The course aims to provide NTU undergraduate students with the basic skills and knowledge required to learn how to swim. Participants will learn the correct techniques required to swim the four strokes (frontcrawl, backstroke, butterfly and breaststroke). Skills like threading water, plunges/starts and turns/somersaults will be taught. In addition, FINA rules relating to these strokes will be introduced.

Students who read SS9401 Aquatics cannot read SS9402 Introductory Swimming.
